text:
mike: Heads-up from chaos run: during simulated eu->apac failover, several warm nodes failed to decrypt model shards. It surfaced a surprising interaction between per-region KMS policies and our fallback routing.
anya: Error log?
mike: ```
DecryptError: key_not_found
  key_id: projects/redwood/keys/model-enc-eu-2025
  attempted_by: apac-node-17
  reason: "access denied by key policy: allow_use_in_region==eu-west"
```
li: So apac node attempted to unwrap the model key but was blocked by key policy. Why was the node asked to load a region-encrypted artifact?
zahra: Because our fallback routing doesn't currently validate `artifact.encryption.policy` vs `node.kms_scope` before attempting load; it only checks residency for weights, not encryption scoping.
ops-bot: ops-bot: note: some customers require keys to never leave EU and forbid wrapped-key export; they were marked `kms: region-locked` in tenant manifest.
anya: If keys are region-locked we cannot copy or unwrap outside region. Options: (1) avoid routing to regions that cannot access the key (policy-check routing), (2) use ephemeral region-scoped wrapping keys that are derived in-region (requires in-region unwrap then re-wrap, possibly illegal under some contracts), (3) keep pre-warmed standby nodes in-region with pre-unwrapped cache of symmetric keys (key-in-memory lifetime constraints), (4) use delegated HSM signing where an external proxy mediates decryption without exporting key.
mike: Delegated HSM proxy is interesting: apac node would call eu HSM to decrypt but eu HSM policy may block remote RPCs. Also adds network latency and introduces cross-region crypto calls.
li: For customers forbidding cross-border key use, probably only option 1 and 3 are viable: either never route off-region, or keep a dedicated in-region pre-warmed standby with the unwrapped key loaded into a secure enclave for the duration of the reservation. But that increases cost.
zahra: Edge-case: Private deployments (on-prem) may use customer-managed KMS with HSM that refuses any external requests; then we must ensure failover doesn't try to access that artifact.
anya: We should add `encryption: {"scope":"region-locked|global|customer-owned"}` in manifest. Proxy preflight can check node.kms_capabilities against artifact.encryption.scope and `tenant.residency`. If mismatch -> consult fallback policy.
mike: Agreed. Also need operator runbook: when `decrypt.blocked_by_kmspolicy` happens, do not auto-forward to that node. Instead return `X-Redwood-Degraded: encryption_blocked` and metric `failover.encryption_mismatch`. Call flow: 1) proxy preflight artifact metadata, 2) confirm node.kms_capabilities includes `can_unwrap:key_id` or `can_delegate_decrypt`, 3) allow load else apply fallback.
zahra: We must also add telemetry fields: `artifact.encryption_scope`, `key.signed_by`, `key.policy_flags` and `node.kms_region`, `node.hsm_available` in health checks. Operators need a clear mapping UI.
li: For longer-term: consider introducing a wrapped-key rotation protocol: publish `artifact.wrapped_key_versions` for each region and a signed `wrap-policy` that allows an in-region KMS to unwrap once and rewrap under a region-local key (if customer consents). That lets us pre-provision region-specific wrapped keys without moving raw key material.
anya: Important: legal says any path that does rewrap must have explicit customer consent and audit trail.
legal: legal: confirm: if we implement rewrap-for-failover we require (A) per-tenant opt-in, (B) signed consent with timestamp, (C) immutable logs + operator id for each rewrap operation. We'll need to surface this in dashboard and API.
mike: Also propose feature flags: `preflight-enforce-encryption` and `allow-rewrap-emergency` (default off). Ops can enable per-tenant for recovery drills.
zahra: Implementation notes: 1) Model build pipeline must publish `encryption.manifest.json` with `encrypted_shard_paths`, `wrap_policy`, `allowed_regions`, `wrapped_key_version_map`. 2) Proxy preflight API call `GET /artifact/meta/{id}` returns those fields. 3) Runtime health check advertises `kms_capabilities` and `hsm_latency_estimate`.
li: Add small pseudo to proxy preflight: ```
meta = GET /artifact/meta/{id}
if meta.encryption.scope == "region-locked" and node.kms_region != meta.allowed_region: block_forward("encryption_scope_mismatch")
if meta.encryption.scope == "global" and not node.kms_capable: block_forward("node_no_kms")
```
anya: For immediate mitigation: ops, please add the preflight check for encryption scope to the proxy feature-flag rollout and pause any cross-region failover tests against region-locked tenants until it's on.
ops-bot: ops-bot: feature-flag `preflight-enforce-encryption` created and set to `on` for staging cluster. Pausing cross-region failover for tenants with `encryption.scope==region-locked`.
mike: I'll file an RFC: problem statement, manifest schema, short-term preflight policy, metrics (`failover.encryption_mismatch`, `rewrap.requests`, `rewrap.failures`), and a runbook. I'll cc legal and security. ETA draft: 72h.
zahra: I'll prototype the manifest additions and a sample wrapped_key_version_map format. Example snippet to include in RFC: ```
{
  "artifact_id":"gen-v4-large:2026-01-05",
  "encryption":{
    "scope":"region-locked",
    "allowed_region":"eu-west",
    "wrap_policy":"no_rewrap",
    "wrapped_key_version_map":{
      "eu-west":"wkv-v12",
      "us-east":"wkv-v12-us"
    }
  }
}
```
li: Nice. Also add test harness to simulate HSM RPC latencies so we can measure impact if we ever go the delegated-decrypt route.
mike: Thanks all. Legal, please add required consent language; security, we need threat model for in-memory unwrapped keys in standby. Ops, roll the preflight flag to prod after staging verification.
legal: Will prepare consent template.
ops-bot: ops-bot: staging preflight flag verified; scheduled rollout window TBD.
mike: End of thread.
